From: Danielle Brooks <danielle.brooks@cruxanalytics.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: sre-ops@cruxanalytics.com
Date: Tue, 2 Jul 2028 09:17:00 -0400
Subject: Urgent: sustained 5xx/429 on /v1/generate - impacting batch jobs

Laura —

We started seeing a sustained burst of 5xx and 429 responses to our /v1/generate endpoint starting ~08:58 ET this morning. It’s hitting all our nightly batch workers and causing timeouts/retries that are compounding the problem. Sample error lines attached.

Key impact:
- 5xx and 429 peaked at ~24% error rate between 08:58–09:10 ET.
- Our backoff/retry logic is causing many duplicate inflight requests.
- We are on a Dedicated pool (crux-prod-pool) — this looks like capacity exhaustion and slow autoscale.

Can you confirm immediate mitigation (rate limiting, emergency scaling, fallback model) and an ETA for stabilization? This is blocking our production reports.

Thanks,
Danielle
Danielle Brooks
SRE, Crux Analytics

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 2 Jul 2028 10:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Fwd: Urgent: sustained 5xx/429 on /v1/generate - impacting batch jobs

Quick diagnostic and actions taken (summary):
- Root observation: the crux-prod-pool exhibited persistent queue growth on GPU nodes; metrics show full GPU util and KV cache pressure starting 08:56 ET. Autoscaler decision loop was delayed by ~90s due to throttled control-plane calls to the Dedicated controller during a cross-customer spike.
- Immediate mitigations executed (10:00–10:03 ET):
  * Pushed emergency +4 GPUs to crux-prod-pool (warm nodes prepped and attached).
  * Enabled aggressive autoscale padding for the pool for 1 hour to avoid rapid re-evaporation.
  * Deployed model-fallback for Crux traffic: 12% of requests now route to quantized-medium model (lower mem footprint, slightly lower quality).
  * Turned on per-customer circuit-breaker to return 429 early for high-concurrency clients — this reduces retry amplification.
- Current status: error rate dropped from 24% -> 3.2% over 7 minutes after actions. Latency tail improved but some residual retry storms remain.

Next asks:
- Marcus: can you confirm logs/trace capture for the 09:00–09:10 window and push a snapshot to the postmortem drive.
- Laura/Marissa: please communicate the temporary steps taken and proposed customer remediation (credit + timeline for full RCA).

I’ll follow-up with a runbook update to avoid the delayed controller-loop issue.

— Karthik
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the quick escalation. I just spoke with your SREs — appreciate the sample logs. They confirmed the impact on nightly pipelines and want a written remediation plan plus credits for the affected window.

- Near-term: we will adjust default client guidance to recommend linear backoff and honor per-request priority headers to reduce amplification.
- RCA/postmortem: full write-up within 5 business days; follow-up call scheduled if you want to walk through findings.

Laura, can you confirm approvals for a goodwill credit up to $12k and the priority monitoring add-on? Ben, looped for sign-off on the credit.

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 3 Jul 2028 16:48:00 -0400
Subject: RE: Urgent: sustained 5xx/429 on /v1/generate - impacting batch jobs — stabilization summary and next steps

Looping back with a brief summary and next steps now that the immediate spike is contained.

What we saw: transient Dedicated pool resource exhaustion combined with a brief control-plane throttling event that delayed autoscale decisions. This allowed a retry-amplification loop from client-side batch retries to drive a short-lived 5xx/429 burst.

What we did: emergency capacity (+4 GPUs), model-fallback routing (12%), per-customer circuit-breaker, and aggressive pool padding. Error rate returned to baseline; customer pipelines are back to normal.

Customer ask and business decision: Approved a $10k goodwill credit and one month of priority infra monitoring. Marissa will send the contract amendment.

Follow-ups (owners):
- Postmortem write-up with timeline, root cause, and permanent mitigations — Karthik (RCA draft in 3 business days).
- Controller/Autoscaler fix to prevent throttled-decision loops — Marcus/Early-Infra (plan in 5 business days).
- Client guidance updates and SDK backoff defaults — Product + DevEx (Marissa to own customer comms).

Danielle — thanks for your patience and for sending the traces. We’ll share the postmortem and improvements as they land.

Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Success — Redwood Inference
